newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks close higher, Bancoquia soars.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks close higher, Bancoquia soars.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed higher on Friday after a day of active trading that was fueled, in part, by rumors that a Spanish bank was planning to form a strategic partnership with Medellin-based Banco Comercial Antioqueno (Bancoquia).

Bogota's IBB rose 0.17 percent to close at 830.31 on a trading volume of 2.19 billion pesos while Medellin's IBOMED general price index ended up 0.11 percent at 13,217.18. Volume in Medellin was 2.8 billion pesos.
"There was real demand from local investors for Bancoquia," one Bogota-based broker said.
"This may have been because of rumors, that have circulated all day but haven't been confirmed, of a possible investment by Banco Santander de Espaa in the bank," he said.

Spokesmen for Bancoquia, Colombia's eighth largest bank and the financial arm of Santo Domingo industrial conglomerate, could not be reached for immediate comment. But the bank's stock jumped 8.10 percent in Bogota to close at its high for the year of 2,000 pesos per share.
In Medellin, Bancoquia rose 5.88 percent to also close at 2,000 pesos.

Other winners included retailer Almancenes Exito, which rose 1.69 percent on large cross trades in Medellin to end at 3,000 pesos per share. Cement maker Cementos Argos edged up 0.10 percent in Medellin, closing at 5,195 pesos a share.

Brokers said cross trading in Bogota accounted for a huge 65 percent jump in the shares of Corporacion Financiera de Caldas, which ended at 597 pesos a share. They attributed the rise to year-end position squaring by major shareholders in the company but said the stock is so thinly-traded that its leap upward had little or no effect on the overall price index.
